original_question: In a 4-uniform hypergraph with distinguished nodes s and t, suppose one must separate s from t while minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits and forbidding every 2-vs-2 split; equivalently, consider the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem obtained as the limit w_2 -> infinity with w_1 = 1. What is the computational complexity of this problem?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 3.2 in Section 3: "What is the complexity of the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target very closely. It correctly identifies the 4-uniform hypergraph setting with distinguished source/sink vertices s and t, the objective of minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits, the prohibition of all 2-vs-2 splits, and the fact that this is the w1 = 1, w2 -> infinity special case of the broader cardinality-based 4-uniform hypergraph s-t cut problem.
missing_details: State formally that the optimization is over all bipartitions {S, V \ S} with s in S and t in V \ S.
Define the cut-type notation used in the paper: ∂i(S) = {e in E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V \ S)|) = i}.
Specify explicitly that H = (V, E) is a finite 4-uniform hypergraph, i.e. every hyperedge has exactly four vertices.

Make clear that this is the cardinality-based cut model with w0 = 0, unit penalty on every 1-vs-3 split, and 2-vs-2 splits excluded via the no-even-split constraint (equivalently, infinite penalty in the limiting discussion).
Sharpen the phrase "computational complexity" to the paper’s intended unresolved dichotomy: whether the optimization problem is NP-hard or instead admits a polynomial-time algorithm.
refined_question: Let H = (V, E) be a finite 4-uniform hypergraph with source vertex s and sink vertex t. For a bipartition {S, V \ S} with s in S and t in V \ S, define ∂i(S) = {e in E : min(|e ∩ S|, |e ∩ (V \ S)|) = i}. What is the computational complexity of solving the optimization problem min{|∂1(S)| : S ⊆ V, s in S, t in V \ S, and ∂2(S) = empty set}? In other words, is the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem polynomial-time solvable, or is it NP-hard?
justification: The nearest official target is Open Problem 3.2, not the broader Open Problem 3.1. Section 3 first defines the cardinality-based hypergraph s-t cut objective in equation (1), then states Open Problem 3.1 for 4-uniform hypergraphs with w1 = 1 and w2 > 2. Immediately afterward, the paper isolates the special case obtained by taking w2 to infinity with w1 fixed at 1, names it the No-Even-Split 4-uniform s-t cut problem, and describes it exactly as minimizing the number of 1-vs-3 hyperedge splits while making no 2-vs-2 splits. Open Problem 3.2 then asks precisely for the computational complexity of that problem. The surrounding discussion also clarifies that the intended question is whether the problem is NP-hard or instead has a polynomial-time algorithm.
